idea.description: Test an explicitly balanced mixture of uniform random-prefix terminal-mask examples and baseline random-mask examples within the supplied corrected BERT4Rec. Separate loss-normalization effects from masking effects before attributing any gain. Train exactly one independent model per category and retain appended-mask inference.
idea.motivation: Terminal examples remove the future context available in interior reconstruction and align supervision with prediction. This may reduce two user-facing failures: treating older interests as continuing demand and ranking weak, broadly related matches above choices supported by the immediate context. These are hypotheses rather than demonstrated remedies: uniform original-position sampling does not explicitly favor recent events, and histories alone cannot establish ownership, compatibility, or incremental usefulness. Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics show weaker training-exposed margins, motivating a test of endpoint ranking, but their margins do not establish the mechanism or held-out improvement.
idea.implementation_notes:
Start from the supplied corrected BERT4Rec without inspecting other trials or reusing their checkpoints. Preserve the baseline architecture, loss function, negative count and distribution, optimizer, user-sampling distribution, initialization seed, and update count. Define the experiment as endpoint alignment rather than recency weighting.

Normalization control: determine the supplied baseline's actual reduction from its provided code. If it averages all supervised tokens together, first compare that baseline with per-example averaging using identical sampled histories, corrupted inputs, targets, negatives, and update schedule. These are separate single-model trials, never fused. The primary masking comparison must use the same per-example reduction in control and treatment. For the treatment, construct equal-sized terminal and random branches and use loss = 0.5 * mean(terminal example losses) + 0.5 * mean(random example losses). Each example loss is the mean over its valid supervised positions. With an odd batch size, use a declared seeded alternating allocation and separate branch means. Equal coefficients do not imply equal gradient norms. Do not silently change normalization and attribute the entire difference to terminal masking.

For terminal examples, sample a cutoff j uniformly from 1 through len(history)-1 using zero-based indexing, requiring at least one preceding interaction. The target is history[j]; retain history[max(0,j-(L-1)):j], append the reserved MASK, and left-pad to L. Never include the target event or any later event. Earlier occurrences of the same item remain valid historical context. Random-mask examples retain corrected baseline corruption with supervised targets hidden; ensure every example has at least one valid supervised target. Use the same eligible user distribution in the normalization-matched comparison, explicitly reporting any exclusions required by histories shorter than two events. Continue the baseline negative sampler and its existing exclusions unchanged; document their exact behavior rather than silently introducing full-history exclusions or a different proposal.

The primary mixture also changes available context and supervised-target count, so it cannot isolate target placement alone. Record branch example counts, supervised-target counts, original cutoffs, retained/visible context lengths, corruption counts, and optional sampled branch gradient norms. Record provenance separately without changing the loader's (None, sequence, positive, negative) contract. If budget permits, a separate one-target control compares terminal-only, exactly-one-random-mask, and their mixture using matched user and pre-corruption sequence-length distributions; future-context availability remains an intentional treatment difference. Further controls can hold corrupted inputs fixed and supervise either all masked positions or one uniformly selected mask: with per-example normalization their expected gradients agree, but variance differs. A separate one-mask-versus-multiple-mask comparison with one supervised target measures corruption effects. Target-budget matching is an additional experiment, not interchangeable with the required fixed-update comparison. Defer recency-weighted endpoints, positional biases, and negative-hardness changes until endpoint alignment is assessed.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, exactly 200 batches per epoch, and at most 200 epochs. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; save artifacts beneath the trial directory. Execute single-GPU within the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget. Predeclare the 50% mixture, comparisons, and unchanged host-compatible checkpoint-selection rule before observing their validation outcomes. Each trial trains one model per category; prediction loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category, without averaging, independently fitted auxiliary scores, or fusion.

Preserve ModelView, log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Retain the four-tuple diagnostic loader and return measured metrics with definitions. Distinguish terminal and interior training margins when provenance is available; otherwise mark that distinction unavailable. Training-exposed margins and omitted history-sensitivity results cannot establish held-out gains or a preferred recency direction. Embedding alignment near 0.5 alone does not establish collapse or representation quality. Sampler provenance, fresh-process predictor parity, and attention-deletion checks remain unavailable until genuinely implemented and measured. Preserve existing diagnostic fixtures and add provenance or parity checks only through supported interfaces.

The embedded predictor writer must reproduce the trained architecture, ID mapping, category routing, reserved token IDs, and appended-mask construction. Truncate history to L-1 before appending MASK. Find the last nonpadding position from actual indices, never count-1. A fresh-process reload and score comparison is needed before claiming checkpoint/predictor parity; live-model checks alone are insufficient. Restrict information to public histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps. Do not use unavailable ratings, review text, item categories/prices/stores, simulator traits, held-out target timestamps, or test files.

Label the host metric sampled HR@10: one positive plus 99 unique negatives, 200 validation users/category, evaluation seed 42. Report each category's hits/200 and HR@10, its difference from baseline, and the equally weighted macro difference. One extra hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. If the host supplies paired user-level outcomes, compute a category-stratified paired bootstrap with 10,000 resamples and analysis seed 42, resampling 200 user pairs within each category while retaining fixed candidate outcomes; report the percentile 95% interval for the macro difference. Intervals condition on fitted models, categories, and candidates and exclude training-seed variability, candidate-sampling variability, and adaptive selection. Set preprocessing_seed=0 and training_seed=42.
Declare mixture=0.5, fixed hyperparameters, comparisons, and checkpoint rule.
Use only supplied training histories and unchanged host validation.

Normalization control, if baseline uses pooled token averaging:
    Compare baseline reduction versus per-example reduction.
    Reuse identical sampled examples, masks, negatives, and update schedule.
    Train separate models; never combine their predictions.

Primary comparison: normalized random-mask control versus normalized mixture.
For each required category:
    Initialize one supplied corrected BERT4Rec with seed 42.
    For each epoch, at most 200:
        For each of exactly 200 batches:
            Sample eligible users with the declared baseline-compatible distribution.
            For mixture treatment, assign exactly half to each branch.
            For normalized control, use baseline random masking throughout.
            For each terminal example with history h:
                j = seeded_uniform_integer(1, len(h)-1)  # inclusive
                prefix = h[max(0, j-(L-1)):j]
                sequence = left_pad(prefix + [MASK], L)
                positive = zeros(L); positive[L-1] = h[j]
                negative = unchanged_baseline_negative_sampler(h, target=h[j])
                Record cutoff, original target position, and corruption provenance.
            For each random example:
                sequence, positive, negative = corrected_baseline_masking(h)
                Require at least one supervised reserved-mask position.
            Compute unchanged unreduced loss at valid supervised positions.
            example_loss = mean(valid position losses within each example)
            If treatment:
                loss = 0.5*mean(terminal example_loss)
                     + 0.5*mean(random example_loss)
            Else:
                loss = mean(example_loss)
            Update the single network using the unchanged optimizer.
            Record branch counts, target counts, and context-length summaries.
    Select and save one checkpoint using the declared host-compatible rule.
Write the matching category-routed predictor and model configuration.

For prediction:
    Load exactly one checkpoint for the requested category.
    sequence = left_pad(history[-(L-1):] + [MASK], L)
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
    index = max(position where sequence[position] != PAD)
    scores = model.predict_score(features[index], candidate_items)
Verify reload parity through a fresh-process runner if available.

Obtain sampled HR@10 only from the unchanged host evaluator.
Report category hits, category differences, and macro difference.
If paired user outcomes are supplied:
    Use 10,000 seed-42 category-stratified paired bootstrap resamples.
    Report percentile 95% interval with conditional-uncertainty limitations.
Disclose every evaluated trial/checkpoint and freeze final selection.

evolution_history.description: Increase terminal-mask supervision within the corrected BERT4Rec, testing endpoint recency separately from training-negative count and loss changes. Train exactly one independent model per category, preserving the bidirectional masked-item backbone and appended-mask inference.
evolution_history.motivation: The proposal explicitly targets two reported user failures: historical interests outweighing present priorities, and broadly plausible recommendations displacing stronger specific next choices. Recent endpoints emphasize more current observations, while terminal supervision removes future context and trains the actual next-choice task. These mechanisms provide hypotheses rather than evidence of improved compatibility, ownership awareness, duplication avoidance, or mood inference. Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have negative tenth-percentile margins and wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%, motivating evaluation of lower-tail discrimination. Near-zero mean item-embedding cosine similarity provides no reason to prioritize an anti-collapse intervention.
evolution_history.implementation_notes:
Modify the host-supplied corrected baseline rather than reconstructing its unavailable implementation. Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, and single-GPU execution per trial. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory and never read other trials or checkpoints. Preserve the host optimizer, updates and baseline objective for the initial masking/endpoint comparison. Do not silently replace a different baseline loss with pairwise logistic loss; declare that replacement as a separate experimental factor.

Define a training history H=(x_1,...,x_n), with n>=2. Uniformly sample eligible users, then sample endpoint t in {2,...,n} before truncation. The uniform condition uses P(t)=1/(n-1); the exponential condition uses P(t) proportional to 2^(-(n-t)/10), equivalently alpha=2^(-1/10), approximately 0.9330. The ten-interaction half-life is a proposed setting, not a validated result. Retain the earlier 50% uniform/50% exponential endpoint mixture as an optional, separately declared follow-up rather than conflating it with the primary exponential condition. Sample the terminal branch independently with q=0.5; reconstruction-only uses q=0.

For terminal examples, input is left_pad(last_{L-1}(x_1,...,x_{t-1})+[MASK], L), label x_t. Exclude the target occurrence and entire suffix; legitimate earlier repetitions may remain. In zero-based code, use H[:t] and target H[t] with t sampled from {1,...,n-1}. For reconstruction examples, use the training-only prefix H[:t+1] under that indexing, retain its last L items, select each nonpadding position independently with probability 0.15, and force one uniformly selected nonpadding target if none is selected. Replace every selected occurrence with the reserved MASK token; do not leave selected targets unchanged. Reconstruction permits bidirectional context within this prefix, as BERT4Rec intends. Do not introduce shifted next-item labels at unmasked positions.

The initial comparison crosses reconstruction-only versus q=0.5 terminal mixture with uniform versus exponential endpoints. This estimates the terminal-mixture effect, endpoint effect and their interaction under a common sampling protocol. The q=0 uniform cell is a controlled reconstruction reference; if its preprocessing differs from the supplied cold start, report that distinction and retain a cold-start comparison when budget permits. At 0% progress, prefer this small controlled study to immediately adding text encoders or hard-negative mining.

For the proposed pairwise-loss extension, draw IID uniform negatives with replacement from real item IDs excluding every known training positive for that user; exclude padding and MASK. Sample 32 negatives per supervised target. Replacement permits K=32 even for small eligible pools, with repeated draws counted as draws. Skip a target if its eligible pool is empty and report the count. Excluding known positives reduces a specific source of false negatives but cannot identify all unobserved preferences. The earlier suggestion to reduce K for small pools is an alternative without-replacement protocol, not the primary IID experiment, and requires separate reporting.

Compute mean pairwise softplus across negatives, then targets within each example, then examples. This prevents examples with more reconstruction targets from receiving greater total weight merely because of target count; q controls their expected share of example loss, although not gradient magnitude. Original BERT4Rec instead averages valid targets across the batch; per-target normalization is a separate ablation. For L_K=mean_k softplus(s_neg_k-s_pos), IID sampling gives the same conditional expected gradient at K=1 and K=32, with negative-sampling gradient covariance reduced by 1/K conditional on the example, parameters and forward randomness. It does not reduce all user, masking or dropout variability. Stronger discrimination is therefore a possible optimization outcome, not a stronger population objective. Pairwise logistic loss remains AUC-oriented and does not directly optimize HR@10.

Candidate softmax, log(1+sum_k exp(s_neg_k-s_pos)), is a distinct objective for K>1; it exponentially emphasizes stronger competitors. A subsequent comparison can cross pairwise versus candidate softmax with K in {1,32}. No logQ correction is required for the specified uniform pairwise objective. Importance-corrected sampled softmax is another separate formulation with generally biased finite-sample gradients; deterministic hard selection cannot inherit uniform proposal probabilities.

Predeclare configurations, contrasts, checkpoint-selection and stopping rules, and GPU allocations before observing their scores. Use the host's existing checkpoint-selection procedure; if none is supplied, declare a fixed validation schedule and choose the highest macro-validation checkpoint with earliest-epoch tie breaking. Every complete comparison must retain all four categories. Count training, failures and diagnostics against 43,200 GPU-seconds; four slots reduce elapsed time, not GPU cost. Reserve budget for complete four-category comparisons and stop launching configurations when their estimated completion cost exceeds the remaining allocation. Compare both fixed-update quality and, only when budget permits, an equal-GPU-time follow-up; record actual GPU-seconds. Avoid attributing bundled improvements to individual components.

Select only using the pinned macro validation HR@10. If the host exposes per-user hits without evaluator changes, report category deltas, discordant paired hits and a paired bootstrap interval: resample 200 paired user records with replacement within each category, recompute the equally weighted macro difference, and use the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of 10,000 replicates with bootstrap seed 42. One changed hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. These intervals condition on trained models and candidate sets; they do not quantify training-seed variability, candidate-sampling variability or winner-selection bias. Treat gains as exploratory, freeze the chosen configuration before held-out evaluation, and do not infer full-catalog gains from 99-negative evaluation.

Recency weighting can overfit final training positions or underrepresent persistent interests; q=0.5 retains reconstruction supervision, and the uniform condition measures this risk. Additional negatives can increase runtime without changing the expected pairwise objective. Do not use item popularity, sequence length or recent position as evidence of compatibility. Unidentified simulator items are unassessable feedback, not explicit content rejection; do not construct preference labels from them.

Inference loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category, appends MASK after the last L-1 observed items, and reads the final nonpadding position using positions or the final appended-mask index, never count-1 on left-padded histories. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items). Update the embedded predictor writer whenever architecture, configuration or inference behavior changes, preserving checkpoint consistency. Never score padding or MASK as recommendation candidates.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and the host ModelView interfaces, with view.model referencing the trained nn.Module. Adapt family-specific sample_batch so positive labels correspond to actually masked positions; do not feed shifted labels through visible bidirectional inputs. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), all B x L. Measure margins only at valid hidden targets. Hold the diagnostic masking, sampling and aggregation protocol fixed across compared models or explicitly flag incomparable measurements. Return measured metrics and their definitions, with no invented category breakdowns. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; review text, ratings, categories, prices, stores and simulator traits are unavailable.

        for epoch in range(max_epochs_at_most_200):
            for step in range(200):
                losses = []
                for H in uniformly_sampled_eligible_training_users:
                    # Zero-based target index; endpoint sampled before truncation.
                    t = sample_index(1, len(H)-1, uniform_or_exponential_half_life_10)
                    if Bernoulli(q):
                        sequence = left_pad(H[:t][-(L-1):] + [MASK], L)
                        positions = [final_nonpadding_position(sequence)]
                        targets = [H[t]]
                    else:
                        sequence = left_pad(H[:t+1][-L:], L)
                        positions = bernoulli_nonpadding_positions(sequence, probability=0.15)

                        targets = copy(sequence[positions])
                        sequence[positions] = MASK
                    features = model.log2feats(sequence)[positions]
                    if initial_controlled_comparison:

                    else:

                        example_loss = mean_targets(target_losses)
                    losses.append(example_loss)

            apply_predeclared_host_validation_and_checkpoint_policy()
        save_exactly_one_selected_checkpoint_with_configuration(category)

    record_configuration_cost_failures_and_category_results()

## Insights and directions

**Starting point.** (1) Appended-mask prediction uses preceding events; interior reconstruction can exploit later events. Terminal supervision tests this mismatch. (2) Users report stale-interest recommendations and weak, broadly related matches. Endpoint training may address these failures, but uniform cutoffs do not preferentially sample recent original events. (3) Industrial and Electronics have negative tenth-percentile training margins (−0.2267 and −0.0479). These show ranking weaknesses, without establishing their cause or held-out impact.

**Related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec §3.6](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) describes last-item training examples without specifying their ratio; its released generator does not establish a dedicated terminal-training mixture. (2) [RSS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) distinguishes uniform from recency-weighted sampling. Neither establishes the best schedule here. (3) [Loss comparisons](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07602) motivate fixed objectives and negatives; loss reduction also changes example weighting. (4) [Sampled-metric research](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) limits conclusions to the pinned candidate protocol.

## Framework and candidate ideas

| Direction | Intervention | Intended gap |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision alignment | Fixed terminal-mask mixture | Interior recovery versus endpoint prediction |
| Temporal representation | Learned relative-position attention bias | Persistent versus current interests |
| Ranking supervision | Moderately hard negatives | Weak positive–negative separation |

Scores are prospective. O/P/U/M/D denote originality, potential, user alignment, model alignment, and difficulty; higher D means harder. Each cell states a strength and limitation.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed terminal mixture | 3: controlled adaptation; established principle | 7: useful baseline; uncertain gains | 6: context alignment; no recency guarantee | 6: endpoint separation; cause unproven | 4: sampler change; controls matter |
| Learned positional bias | 5: flexible relevance; familiar mechanism | 7: retains older signals; overfitting risk | 7: contextual fit; ownership unknown | 5: changes attention; sensitivity unavailable | 6: few parameters; writer changes |
| Moderate-hard negatives | 4: focused ranking; established sampling | 7: difficult distinctions; false negatives | 5: sharper ranks; relevance uncertain | 8: addresses margins; training evidence | 6: single network; proposal correction |

## Selected experiment: fixed terminal-mask mixture

At 10% progress, retain the simplest intervention: exactly 50% terminal-prefix examples, otherwise baseline random masking. Uniformly sample eligible training cutoffs, replace targets with the reserved mask, and discard later events. Preserve bidirectional prefix attention.

Hypotheses target **older interests treated as continuing demand** and **weak, broadly related matches**, plus weak masked-target separation. Endpoint alignment could help; explicit recency, compatibility, redundancy, and causal preferences remain unestablished.

# Each invocation trains one configuration and one model per category.
# Default treatment: exactly half terminal examples, per-example BPR.
# Matched masking control: BERT4REC_MASKING=random, reduction=per_example.
# Normalization control: BERT4REC_MASKING=random, reduction=token.
# The two random controls use identical sampling code and random draws.
# Checkpoint selection remains first strict improvement in validation HR@10.
MASKING_MODE = os.environ.get("BERT4REC_MASKING", "mixture")
LOSS_REDUCTION = os.environ.get("BERT4REC_LOSS_REDUCTION", "per_example")
RECONSTRUCTION_MASK_PROBABILITY = 0.15

    raise ValueError("BERT4REC_MASKING must be mixture or random")
if LOSS_REDUCTION not in {"per_example", "token"}:
    raise ValueError("BERT4REC_LOSS_REDUCTION must be per_example or token")
if MASKING_MODE == "mixture" and LOSS_REDUCTION != "per_example":
    raise ValueError("The balanced mixture requires per-example normalization")


def sample_batch(
    user_train: dict[int, list[int]], itemnum: int, batch_size: int, maxlen: int
):
    if maxlen < 2 or batch_size < 1:
        raise ValueError("maxlen must be at least two and batch_size positive")
    if MASKING_MODE == "mixture" and batch_size < 2:
        raise ValueError("The balanced mixture requires batch_size >= 2")
    users = [u for u, items in user_train.items() if len(items) >= 2]
    if not users:
        raise RuntimeError("no users with at least two training interactions")
    # Alternate the larger branch for odd batches; never infer branch identity
    # from target counts, since random masking can also select a single target.
    call_index = getattr(sample_batch, "call_index", 0)
    terminal_count = 0
    if MASKING_MODE == "mixture":
        terminal_count = batch_size // 2 + (batch_size % 2) * (call_index % 2)
    sample_batch.call_index = call_index + 1
    sample_batch.last_terminal_count = terminal_count
    batch_seq, batch_pos, batch_neg, provenance = [], [], [], []
    for row in range(batch_size):
        user = random.choice(users)
        history = user_train[user]
        terminal = row < terminal_count
        if terminal:
            endpoint = random.randint(1, len(history) - 1)
            start = max(0, endpoint - (maxlen - 1))
            # Target and all later events are absent from the input context.
            items = history[start:endpoint] + [history[endpoint]]
        else:
            endpoint = len(history) - 1
            start = max(0, len(history) - maxlen)
            # Random reconstruction uses the complete retained training window,
            # without the previous recency-weighted prefix selection.
            items = history[start:]
        seq = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        pos = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        neg = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        seq[-len(items) :] = items
        offset = maxlen - len(items)
        eligible = list(range(offset, maxlen))
        if terminal:
            selected = [maxlen - 1]
        else:
            selected = [
                i for i in eligible if random.random() < RECONSTRUCTION_MASK_PROBABILITY
            ]
            if not selected:
                selected = [random.choice(eligible)]
        # Preserve rejection sampling of one uniform catalog negative per target,
        # excluding every item in this user's full supplied training history.
        interacted = set(history)
        if len(interacted) >= itemnum:
            raise RuntimeError("no unobserved negative item available")
        for i in selected:
            pos[i] = seq[i]
            seq[i] = itemnum + 1
            item = random.randint(1, itemnum)
            while item in interacted:
                item = random.randint(1, itemnum)
            neg[i] = item
        branch = "terminal" if terminal else "random"
        provenance.append(
            {
                "user": int(user),
                "branch": branch,
                "cutoff": endpoint,
                "target_positions": [start + i - offset for i in selected],
                "retained_length": len(items),
                "visible_context_length": len(items) - len(selected),
                "corruption_count": len(selected),
            }
        )
        stats = sample_batch.epoch_stats.setdefault(
            branch,
            {
                "examples": 0,
                "targets": 0,
                "cutoff_sum": 0,
                "retained_length_sum": 0,
                "visible_context_length_sum": 0,
                "corruption_count": 0,
            },
        )
        stats["examples"] += 1
        stats["targets"] += len(selected)
        stats["cutoff_sum"] += endpoint
        stats["retained_length_sum"] += len(items)
        stats["visible_context_length_sum"] += len(items) - len(selected)
        stats["corruption_count"] += len(selected)
        batch_seq.append(seq)
        batch_pos.append(pos)
        batch_neg.append(neg)
    # Side-channel provenance preserves the three-array sampler and four-tuple
    # diagnostic-loader interfaces. Only the latest batch is retained in memory.
    sample_batch.last_provenance = provenance
    return np.asarray(batch_seq), np.asarray(batch_pos), np.asarray(batch_neg)

def _history_to_tensor(
    history: list[int], maxlen: int, device: torch.device
) -> torch.Tensor:
    seq_arr = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    for i, item in enumerate(reversed(history[-maxlen:])):
        seq_arr[maxlen - 1 - i] = item
    return torch.tensor([seq_arr], dtype=torch.long, device=device)


def evaluate_val(
    model: nn.Module,
    user_train: dict[int, list[int]],
    user_valid: dict[int, list[int]],
    itemnum: int,
    device: torch.device,
    maxlen: int,
    num_users: int = 200,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Reproducible validation without consuming training randomness
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    val_users = [u for u in user_valid if u in user_train and user_valid[u]]
    if len(val_users) > num_users:
        val_users = rng.sample(val_users, num_users)
    ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
    if not val_users:
        return {"HR@10": 0.0, "HR@20": 0.0, "NDCG@10": 0.0, "NDCG@20": 0.0}

    hr10 = hr20 = ndcg10 = ndcg20 = 0.0
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for user in val_users:
            target = user_valid[user][0]
            history = user_train[user]
            interacted = set(history) | {target, 0}
            ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Fixed unique validation negatives with bounded sampling
            available_count = itemnum - sum(1 <= item <= itemnum for item in interacted)
            if available_count < 99:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"validation user {user} has only {available_count} eligible negatives; "
                    "99 unique negatives are required"
                )
            candidates = [target]
            if available_count < 198:
                available = [
                    item for item in range(1, itemnum + 1) if item not in interacted
                ]
                candidates.extend(rng.sample(available, 99))
            else:
                while len(candidates) < 100:
                    neg_item = rng.randint(1, itemnum)
                    if neg_item not in interacted:
                        interacted.add(neg_item)
                        candidates.append(neg_item)
            ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
            seq_t = _history_to_tensor(history, maxlen, device)
            cand_t = torch.tensor(candidates, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
            scores = model.score_candidates(seq_t, cand_t).detach().cpu().tolist()
            rank = sorted(range(len(scores)), key=lambda i: -scores[i]).index(0)
            hr10 += 1.0 if rank < 10 else 0.0
            hr20 += 1.0 if rank < 20 else 0.0
            ndcg10 += (1.0 / math.log2(rank + 2)) if rank < 10 else 0.0
            ndcg20 += (1.0 / math.log2(rank + 2)) if rank < 20 else 0.0
    n = float(len(val_users))
    model.train()
    return {
        "HR@10": hr10 / n,
        "HR@20": hr20 / n,
        "NDCG@10": ndcg10 / n,
        "NDCG@20": ndcg20 / n,
    }

def bpr_sequence_loss(
    model: nn.Module,
    seq: torch.Tensor,
    pos: torch.Tensor,
    neg: torch.Tensor,
    terminal_count: int | None = None,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    # Branch membership is supplied by the training caller, never inferred
    # from target counts or mutable sampler state inside this function.
    # Diagnostic callers may omit it to obtain ordinary per-example BPR.
    if terminal_count is not None:
        if not 0 <= terminal_count < pos.shape[0]:
            raise ValueError("terminal_count must leave at least one random example")
        if terminal_count > 0 and LOSS_REDUCTION != "per_example":
            raise ValueError("Balanced branches require per-example normalization")

    pos_scores, neg_scores = model(seq, pos, neg)
    valid = pos != 0
    differences = (neg_scores - pos_scores).masked_fill(~valid, 0.0)
    losses = torch.nn.functional.softplus(differences).masked_fill(~valid, 0.0)
    counts = valid.sum(dim=1)
    if LOSS_REDUCTION == "token":
        return losses.sum() / counts.sum().clamp(min=1)

    example_losses = losses.sum(dim=1) / counts.clamp(min=1)
    if terminal_count is not None and terminal_count > 0:
        return (
            0.5 * example_losses[:terminal_count].mean()
            + 0.5 * example_losses[terminal_count:].mean()
        )
    return example_losses.mean()

class BERT4RecModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(
        self,
        itemnum: int,
        hidden_units: int = 64,
        num_blocks: int = 2,
        num_heads: int = 2,
        dropout_rate: float = 0.2,
        maxlen: int = 128,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.itemnum = itemnum
        self.hidden_units = hidden_units
        self.maxlen = maxlen
        self.mask_token = itemnum + 1
        self.item_emb = nn.Embedding(itemnum + 2, hidden_units, padding_idx=0)
        self.pos_emb = nn.Embedding(maxlen + 1, hidden_units, padding_idx=0)
        encoder_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
            d_model=hidden_units,
            nhead=num_heads,
            dim_feedforward=hidden_units * 4,
            dropout=dropout_rate,
            activation="gelu",
            batch_first=True,
            norm_first=True,
        )
        self.encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, num_layers=num_blocks)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_rate)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_units)
        with torch.no_grad():
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.item_emb.weight)
            self.item_emb.weight[0].zero_()
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.pos_emb.weight)
            self.pos_emb.weight[0].zero_()

    def encode_sequence(self, seq: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        batch, length = seq.shape
        pos = torch.arange(length, device=seq.device).unsqueeze(0).expand(batch, -1) + 1
        pos = pos * (seq != 0).long()
        x = self.item_emb(seq) * (self.hidden_units**0.5) + self.pos_emb(pos)
        x = self.dropout(x)
        padding = seq == 0
        safe_padding = padding.clone()
        safe_padding[padding.all(dim=1), -1] = False
        x = self.encoder(x, src_key_padding_mask=safe_padding)
        return self.norm(x)

    def forward(self, seq: torch.Tensor, pos: torch.Tensor, neg: torch.Tensor):
        out = self.encode_sequence(seq)
        pos_scores = (out * self.item_emb(pos)).sum(dim=-1)
        neg_scores = (out * self.item_emb(neg)).sum(dim=-1)
        return pos_scores, neg_scores

    def score_candidates(
        self, seq: torch.Tensor, candidates: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        prediction_seq = torch.zeros_like(seq)
        prediction_seq[:, :-1] = seq[:, 1:]
        prediction_seq[:, -1] = self.mask_token
        out = self.encode_sequence(prediction_seq)
        user_emb = out[0, -1]
        cand_emb = self.item_emb(candidates)
        return torch.matmul(cand_emb, user_emb)

    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        modes = [(module, module.training) for module in self.network.modules()]
        python_rng = random.getstate()
        numpy_rng = np.random.get_state()
        cpu_rng = torch.get_rng_state()
        cuda_rng = torch.cuda.get_rng_state_all() if torch.cuda.is_available() else None
        try:
            self.network.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                integrity = self._integrity()
                collapse = self.analyze_embeddings_collapse_cosine(
                    sample_size=2048, seed=42
                )
                margins, breakdown = (
                    self.analyze_pos_neg_margin_with_category_breakdown(
                        train_loader, num_batches=10, eps=0.5, topk_categories=20
                    )
                )
                required_checks = (
                    "reserved_mask_id_valid",
                    "inference_ids_match",
                    "finite_scores",
                    "live_inference_allclose",
                    "padding_embedding_invariant",
                    "omitted_mask_control_rejected",
                    "count_minus_one_control_rejected",
                )
                failed_checks = [
                    key for key in required_checks if integrity.get(key) is False
                ]
                unavailable_checks = [
                    key for key in required_checks if integrity.get(key) is None
                ]
                if integrity.get("failure"):
                    failed_checks.append("failure")
                # Invalid supervision is a structural failure, even when other
                # positions provide enough observations for finite margins.
                integrity["masked_target_alignment_valid"] = (
                    breakdown["invalid_target_positions"] == 0
                    if breakdown["inspected_batches"] > 0
                    else None
                )
                if integrity["masked_target_alignment_valid"] is False:
                    failed_checks.append("masked_target_alignment_valid")
                elif integrity["masked_target_alignment_valid"] is None:
                    unavailable_checks.append("masked_target_alignment_valid")
                integrity["failed_required_checks"] = failed_checks
                integrity["unavailable_required_checks"] = unavailable_checks
                integrity["structural_status"] = (
                    "FAILED"
                    if failed_checks
                    else (
                        "INCOMPLETE" if unavailable_checks else "OBSERVED_CHECKS_PASSED"
                    )
                )
                integrity["certification_scope"] = (
                    "Observed checks only; sampler provenance, fresh-process predictor "
                    "parity and effective attention-mask inspection remain uncertified."
                )
                sensitivity = (
                    {
                        "exposure": "training-exposed recovery; not held-out generalization",
                        "result": None,
                        "reason": "Skipped because required structural checks failed",
                        "failed_checks": failed_checks,
                        "category_metadata_breakdowns": {},
                    }
                    if failed_checks
                    else self._history_sensitivity()
                )
                metrics = {
                    "bert4rec_integrity": integrity,
                    "embedding_collapse_score": collapse,
                    "embedding_collapse_sample_count": min(
                        2048, int(self.network.itemnum)
                    ),
                    "embedding_collapse_reason": (
                        None
                        if collapse is not None
                        else "Fewer than two item embeddings"
                    ),
                    "pos_neg_margin_mean": margins["mean"],
                    "pos_neg_margin_p10": margins["p10"],
                    "pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate": margins["neg_beats_pos_rate"],
                    "pos_neg_small_margin_rate": margins["small_margin_rate"],
                    "pos_neg_margin_sample_count": margins["count"],
                    "pos_neg_margin_reason": margins["reason"],
                    "pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown": breakdown,
                    "training_history_sensitivity": sensitivity,
                }
                definitions = {
                    "bert4rec_integrity": (
                        "Independent appended-mask fixtures compare exact IDs and live candidate scores "

                        "masked_target_alignment_valid checks that observed supervised positions "
                        "contain reserved masks and valid catalog positive/negative IDs; an empty "
                        "loader makes this check unavailable. It does not certify event provenance."
                    ),
                    "embedding_collapse_score": (
                        "(Mean off-diagonal pairwise cosine + 1)/2 over up to 2048 seed-42 sampled "
                        "catalog embeddings, excluding padding and mask. Measures angular alignment, "
                        "not recommendation diversity or representation quality by itself."
                    ),
                    "embedding_collapse_sample_count": "Number of catalog embeddings sampled",
                    "embedding_collapse_reason": "Reason the collapse statistic is undefined, or null",
                    "pos_neg_margin_mean": "Training-exposed mean positive-minus-negative logit at valid masked targets",
                    "pos_neg_margin_p10": "Training-exposed nearest-rank tenth percentile of masked-target margins",
                    "pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate": "Fraction of valid masked targets with margin < 0",
                    "pos_neg_small_margin_rate": "Fraction of valid masked targets with margin < 0.5",
                    "pos_neg_margin_sample_count": "Number of valid supervised reserved-mask positions observed",
                    "pos_neg_margin_reason": "Reason no valid training margins were observed, or null",
                    "pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown": (
                        "Observed batch, invalid-target and low-margin counts. Category lists remain empty "
                        "because item category metadata is unavailable. The supplied sampler always masks selected targets."
                    ),
                    "training_history_sensitivity": (
                        "One last training target/user with strictly earlier prefix truncated to L-1; "
                        "earlier repeats are retained. Up to 200 users selected with seed 42. "

                        "seed-42 user-bootstrap percentile 95% intervals, conditional on the selected users and "
                        "candidate draw. These intervals exclude checkpoint-selection uncertainty. "

                        "prefix lengths; tied cutpoints may produce empty strata. Results describe training-exposed "
                        "sensitivity, not causal preferences, memorization alone or held-out generalization. "

                    ),
                }
                return {"metrics": metrics, "metric_definitions": definitions}
        finally:
            for module, mode in modes:
                module.training = mode
            random.setstate(python_rng)
            np.random.set_state(numpy_rng)
            torch.set_rng_state(cpu_rng)
            if cuda_rng is not None:
                torch.cuda.set_rng_state_all(cuda_rng)
